items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: And I went back with Al. And I stayed with Al from 47 to 56.

ctx.x: How did you get interested in bass by the way?

Well I always did like bass. I always did like string bass, Dick. And around 1937 after playing the guitar for four years in the band I decided, well you know the bass player with the Al Streaming Band who was the vice president of the Soil Company and had to do all that road traveling. He was told Streaming and he said, Al I'm going to have to quit the band. He said, I got too much traveling. He had been with the band ten years. So he left the band and that's when Al told me, he said, Bob why don't you switch…
But why does Treeman want you on bass? Do you know?

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: Right, I did my share of carnival balls during the Alstream in 19 years.

ctx.x: Yeah, anything that old can hold up. I was going to ask you about carnival balls. That's one thing we never talk much about. You mentioned playing on the truck.

Right, I did my share of carnival balls during the Alstream in 19 years. We had our share of the carnival balls. You know, I played my share of them. I did, you know, the tableau and the supper dance and the whole works. Mm-hmm. For many years, yeah. Al had his portion of it, you know. There was bands like Russ Papalia, Rene Louap, and in the old days, let's see. Johnny Detroit. Bands of that caliber and bands like that, they used to all get a certain percentage of the balls. So I feel like I did my share of them.
Never having seen one in my whole life.
